title: Session / cookies
summary: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, fixation, logout, and session identifiers in URLs.

groups.title: Cookie flags
groups.summary: How the session cookie is issued.

checks.title: Secure on session cookies
checks.why: A session cookie without Secure can be stolen on a plaintext request.
checks.validate: Set-Cookie for the session name lacks Secure on the real login response.

variants.name: Read Set-Cookie on login
variants.payload:
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=tester&password=ChangeMe1!
variants.expect: Every cookie that carries authority must include Secure. Repeat on the first 302.
variants.why: The Secure flag on the session cookie is the transport protection.

variants.name: HTTP Set-Cookie
variants.payload:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A session cookie issued on HTTP is worse. Confirm on port 80 only if HTTP is in scope.
variants.why: A session cookie issued over plaintext HTTP can be stolen on the network.

checks.title: HttpOnly on session cookies
checks.why: A session cookie readable by JavaScript becomes XSS→session theft.
checks.validate: document.cookie contains the session name, or Set-Cookie lacks HttpOnly.

variants.name: Read Set-Cookie
variants.payload:
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=tester&password=ChangeMe1!
variants.expect: Session cookies must include HttpOnly. CSRF tokens may be readable; session ids must not.
variants.why: HttpOnly keeps the session cookie out of script reach.

variants.name: document.cookie
variants.payload: In the logged-in origin console: document.cookie
variants.expect: The session name must be absent. Any other privileged cookie you can read is the same class.
variants.why: A session cookie readable from document.cookie is exposed to any XSS.

checks.title: SameSite matches the real flow
checks.why: SameSite=None without Secure, or Lax when a cross-site POST is the login/CSRF surface.
checks.validate: The issued cookie's SameSite does not match how the app actually authenticates.

variants.name: Read SameSite
variants.payload:
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=tester&password=ChangeMe1!
variants.expect: None requires Secure. Strict breaks top-level OAuth returns. Lax is the usual default — still need a CSRF token on POST.
variants.why: SameSite binds the cookie to the request's site context.

variants.name: Cross-site POST with Lax
variants.expect: Lax should not send the cookie on this POST in modern browsers. A change still happening means the cookie is None or not SameSite.
variants.why: Lax still allows top-level cross-site POSTs, so it is not a CSRF control by itself.

groups.title: Lifecycle
groups.summary: Fixation, logout, and identifiers in URLs.

checks.title: Session fixation / rotation
checks.why: A pre-login cookie that survives authentication lets an attacker plant the session.
checks.validate: The session identifier issued before login is still accepted after login.

variants.name: Compare pre- and post-login cookies
variants.payload: Note Set-Cookie on GET /login, submit credentials, compare the cookie name and value.
variants.expect: Value must change. A new name with the old value still counting is the same bug.
variants.why: The session id must rotate on login; a stable id is the fixation primitive.

variants.name: Planted cookie
variants.payload:
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=wapt-planted-value
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=tester&password=ChangeMe1!
variants.expect: The planted value must not become the authenticated session.
variants.why: Accepting a pre-set session cookie after login means the server did not issue a fresh one.

checks.title: Logout invalidates the server session
checks.why: Logout only deletes the cookie. The old value still works.
checks.validate: A replayed session cookie after logout still returns /me.

variants.name: Replay after logout
variants.payload: Copy the session cookie, log out, send GET /api/v1/me with the old cookie.
variants.why: A session that still works after logout means server-side invalidation is missing.

variants.name: Logout CSRF / missing logout
variants.expect: Forced logout is a finding if there is no CSRF token. Missing logout entirely is a finding too.
variants.why: A missing or CSRF-able logout lets an attacker silently end or hijack the session.

checks.title: Session id in the URL
checks.why: jsessionid=, PHPSESSID=, or a token in the path/query lands in logs and Referer.
checks.validate: A live session identifier is observable in a URL or Referer.

variants.name: Path / query session
variants.payload:
GET /app;jsessionid=<value> HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Rewriting session ids into the URL must be off. Also try ?PHPSESSID= and ?session=.
variants.why: A session id in the URL leaks into logs, history, and Referer.

variants.name: Referer leak
variants.payload: If any URL contains the session id, load a third-party image and inspect Referer.
variants.expect: The identifier must not leave the origin.
variants.why: A session id in the URL reaches a third party via the Referer header.

sess-cookie.purpose: The Secure flag on the session cookie is the transport protection.
sess-cookie.payload:
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=tester&password=ChangeMe1!

doc-cookie.purpose: A session cookie readable from document.cookie is exposed to any XSS.
doc-cookie.payload: In the logged-in origin console: document.cookie
